title: Critique: subjects cannot combine, because points of view cannot

statements.text: A subject is a point of view on a private field of qualities, and points of view exist wholly or not at all. A larger subject that kept its parts as points of view would have to experience red to the exclusion of all else and blue to the exclusion of all else at once. Contents may combine, subjects cannot, so constitutive panpsychism with micro-subjects is ruled out.

sources.quote: it is impossible to explain the constitution of a macro-subject (like one of us) in terms of the assembly of micro-subjects, for, I will argue, subjects cannot combine
Points of view are binary entities: they exist either wholly or not at all.
cannot: this is precluded by the metaphysical logic of points of view
